plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped lilac-pink blooms push straight out of bare ground with no leaves in sight. They carpet damp meadows and fill garden borders just as autumn begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn, peaking from September into October
plants.location: Meadows and gardens across western and central Europe, including the UK, France and Germany
plants.funFact: Autumn crocus is not a true crocus. It is a member of the lily family, and every part of it contains colchicine, a toxic compound that has been used in medicine and in plant breeding.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems burst into clouds of violet-purple daisies with golden centers. The blooms light up roadsides, prairies and wet meadows and are a lifeline for late-season pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through mid-autumn, typically August to October
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from New England to the Great Plains
plants.funFact: Migrating monarch butterflies depend on its nectar to refuel on their long journey south to Mexico.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Spring turns whole streets into tunnels of lavender-blue as trumpet-shaped flowers cover the feathery-leaved trees. When the blossoms drop, they leave a violet carpet on the pavement below.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere, from roughly late September to November
plants.location: Pretoria and Johannesburg in South Africa, and Brisbane and Sydney in Australia
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of the tens of thousands of these trees lining its streets. They are native to South America, not Africa.
